#| label: setup

metrics_path <- file.path("generated", "repo_metrics.csv")
if (!file.exists(metrics_path)) {
  stop("Missing generated repository metrics. Run `just metrics`.", call. = FALSE)
}
metrics_frame <- utils::read.csv(metrics_path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE,
                                 check.names = FALSE)
metrics <- stats::setNames(metrics_frame$value, metrics_frame$metric)

metric_num <- function(key) as.numeric(metrics[[key]])
fmt_int <- function(key) formatC(metric_num(key), format = "d", big.mark = ",")
fmt_num <- function(key, digits = 1L) {
  formatC(metric_num(key), format = "f", digits = digits, big.mark = ",")
}

  format(as.Date(metrics[[key]]), format = format)
}

## A guessing game

<div class="eyebrow">One repository · one maintainer</div>

<div class="hero-question">How many developers—and how many years—would you expect?</div>

::: {.fragment}

Parser. Model compiler. ML, FIML, least squares, ordinal and mixed data.
Information matrices. Robust tests. Simulation machinery. R bindings.

:::

::: {.notes}
Pause and ask the room. Let them supply a number before revealing anything.
The list is illustrative, not intended as a complete capability claim.
:::

## These numbers prove almost nothing

<div class="claim dark">AI makes output cheap. It also makes plausible mistakes cheap.</div>

::: {.fragment}

The scarce work moved:

- from **typing** to specifying the statistical contract;
- from implementing one path to checking every reduction;
- from producing code to designing ways for it to fail.

:::

::: {.fragment}

> The bottleneck moved from implementation to falsification.

:::

::: {.notes}
This is the anti-productivity-flex slide. Volume establishes that the production
function changed; it does not establish scientific value.
:::

## ChatGPT is not the experience I mean

<div class="comparison">
  <div class="quiet">
    <h3>Chat interaction</h3>
    <ul>
      <li>question → answer</li>
      <li>a function or snippet</li>
      <li>you integrate and test it</li>
      <li>context is mostly supplied by you</li>
    </ul>
  </div>
  <div class="accent">
    <h3>Repository agent</h3>
    <ul>
      <li>reads code, rules, tests and history</li>
      <li>edits C++, R, fixtures and docs together</li>
      <li>compiles, runs, diagnoses and revises</li>
      <li>keeps working until the contract closes</li>
    </ul>
  </div>
</div>

<div class="claim">The unit of work is not a prompt. It is a closed development loop.</div>

::: {.notes}
Optional: replace this slide or the next with a 20–30 second recording of one
real Codex turn. Do not do a live demo.
:::

## The loop

<div class="loop">
  <div class="step">Scientific<br>question</div><div class="arrow">→</div>
  <div class="step">Explicit<br>contract</div><div class="arrow">→</div>
  <div class="step">Implementation</div><div class="arrow">→</div>
  <div class="step">Oracle +<br>properties</div><div class="arrow">→</div>
  <div class="step">Simulation</div><div class="arrow">↺</div>
</div>

<div class="full-quote">A coding agent becomes useful when it can travel around this loop—not when it can type the middle box.</div>

::: {.notes}
The contract includes input ordering, scaling, grouping, missingness, supported
combinations and explicit errors. Simulation is allowed to revise the question,
not just approve the implementation.
:::

## AI amplifies architecture

<div class="comparison">
  <div class="accent">
    <h3>Composable repository</h3>
    <ul>
      <li>small inputs and visible data flow</li>
      <li>local contracts and focused tests</li>
      <li>one primitive reused by many methods</li>
      <li>bounded context for both human and agent</li>
    </ul>
  </div>
  <div class="quiet">
    <h3>Coupled repository</h3>
    <ul>
      <li>state hidden in large objects and caches</li>
      <li>string dispatch and distant side effects</li>
      <li>new methods fork the fitting machinery</li>
      <li>the agent produces coherent-looking debt faster</li>
    </ul>
  </div>
</div>

<div class="claim">Good architecture is context engineering.</div>

::: {.notes}
This is not mainly a language claim. An agent reasons better when the dependency
surface is small, contracts are local, and failures occur near their source.
:::

## Why C++ first?

<div class="takeaway-grid">
  <div><strong>One implementation</strong>R exposes thin wrappers; it does not grow a second SEM engine.</div>
  <div><strong>Fast inner loops</strong>Optimization, finite differences and simulation can become routine validation tools.</div>
  <div><strong>Visible contracts</strong>Types, values and <code>std::expected</code> make data flow and failure explicit.</div>
</div>

<div class="claim">Make magmaan less ambitious as a package—and more ambitious as an engine.</div>

::: {.notes}
C++23 is used with no exceptions or RTTI. The point is not macho systems
programming. The point is a fast, typed, binding-independent statistical core.
:::

## A small vocabulary, many compositions

<div class="layer-stack">
  <div class="layer"><div class="name">Friendly API + R</div><div class="desc">thin composition for ordinary workflows</div></div>
  <div class="layer core"><div class="name">Compositional C++</div><div class="desc">spec · data · model · estimate · inference · robust · measures · optim</div></div>
  <div class="layer frontier"><div class="name">Per-domain frontier</div><div class="desc">research methods, still tested, with weaker API-stability promises</div></div>
  <div class="layer"><div class="name">Compatibility boundary</div><div class="desc">lavaan-shaped projection and oracle matching</div></div>
</div>

The extension vocabulary is deliberately small: **discrepancy, optimizer,
standard-error method, fit index, data/moment builder**.

::: {.fragment}

A new method must compose the engine—not fork it.

:::

::: {.notes}
There are many domain types, but few architectural extension ideas. If a method
does not fit, that may reveal a missing abstraction. It is not permission to
create a parallel estimation stack.
:::

## The fitted object is not the program

<div class="branch">
  <div class="fit">Fit<br><span class="tiny">model · data · estimates</span></div>
  <div>information<br>and SEs</div>
  <div>tests and<br>modification indices</div>
  <div>fit measures and<br>standardization</div>
</div>

<br>

Every post-fit choice is an explicit computation with its own configuration,
result and failure.

<div class="comparison small">
  <div class="quiet"><h3>lavaan-style object</h3>Excellent end-user ergonomics: one rich fit, inspect anything.</div>
  <div class="accent"><h3>magmaan engine</h3>Better research ergonomics: inspectable ingredients, replaceable pieces, independent tests.</div>
</div>

::: {.notes}
Be respectful: lavaan optimizes for a different job and is the oracle here. The
claim is that reproducing its mega-object internally would have made magmaan
substantially harder to extend safely with an agent.
:::

## The test corpus is the scientific product

<div class="validation-stack">
  <div class="v1"><span class="number">`r fmt_int("assertions")` assertions</span><span class="desc">local algebra, boundaries, reductions and failure contracts</span></div>
  <div class="v2"><span class="number">finite differences</span><span class="desc">gradients, Jacobians and independent derivative probes</span></div>
  <div class="v3"><span class="number">`r fmt_int("corpus_models")` synthetic models</span><span class="desc">parser → partable → matrices → fit → inference against lavaan</span></div>
  <div class="v4"><span class="number">parity + simulation</span><span class="desc">real data, literature replications, adversarial and boundary cases</span></div>
</div>

<div class="metric-grid">
  <div class="metric"><span class="number">`r fmt_int("test_cases")`</span><span class="label">focused C++ test cases</span></div>
  <div class="metric"><span class="number">`r fmt_int("json_fixtures")`</span><span class="label">frozen JSON fixtures</span></div>
  <div class="metric"><span class="number">`r fmt_int("parity_cases")`</span><span class="label">real-data parity cases</span></div>
  <div class="metric"><span class="number">`r fmt_int("research_notes")`</span><span class="label">LaTeX research notes</span></div>
</div>

::: {.notes}
CI does not need R: oracle output is regenerated deliberately and checked in.
Lavaan is the oracle where parity is claimed. Calling an oracle defect requires
both an independent reference and a violated first-principles property.
:::

## One methods thread, 19–23 June

<div class="timeline">
  <div class="date">19 June</div><div class="event">A numerical jackknife shows the ordinal-DWLS observed-bread gap does <em>not</em> vanish: the estimated-weight influence is missing.</div>
  <div class="date">19 June</div><div class="event">Derive and implement the complete infinitesimal-jackknife sandwich; gate it against resampling and finite differences.</div>
  <div class="date">20–22 June</div><div class="event">Generalize the influence machinery across continuous, ordinal, mixed, multigroup and missing-data paths.</div>
  <div class="date">22 June</div><div class="event">Compose it into RMSEA, CRMR/SRMR, CFI/TLI, modification indices and score tests; add Monte Carlo coverage checks and R surfaces.</div>
  <div class="date">23 June</div><div class="event">Reuse the same casewise influence for one-step case diagnostics.</div>
</div>

<div class="source-line">Timeline reconstructed from git history; dates describe repository history, not uninterrupted wall-clock work.</div>

::: {.notes}
This is the concrete loop: anomaly, mathematical explanation, a reusable
primitive, independent checks, propagation, simulation and interpretation.
:::

## The psychometric result

For ordinal DWLS, the fitted weight Ŵ and the sample moments come from the
**same observations**.

::: {.fragment}

- At exact fit, the extra weight-influence term disappears.
- Under fixed misspecification, it is first order.
- An “observed-Hessian robust SE” is still incomplete if it freezes Ŵ.

:::

<div class="takeaway-grid fragment">
  <div><strong>0.927</strong>coverage from the observed-bread interval</div>
  <div><strong>0.947</strong>coverage from the complete IJ interval</div>
  <div><strong>≈ 0.3%</strong>error in recovered empirical sampling SD</div>
</div>

<div class="source-line">Focused N = 2,500 experiment; nominal coverage 0.95; one structural parameter under misspecification.</div>

::: {.notes}
Do not overgeneralize. This is one controlled design and one focal parameter.
The stronger point for this talk is the full path from discrepancy to tested
method. Source: docs/research/notes/misspec_observed_bread.tex.
:::

## Composition pays compound interest

<div class="claim">Casewise scores + information + a restriction space</div>

<div class="branch">
  <div>robust score tests<br>and MI</div>
  <div>SB / mean–variance<br>adjustments</div>
  <div>eigenvalue mixtures<br>FMG / pEBA</div>
  <div>sign flips · multipliers<br>Hotelling</div>
</div>

<br>

These are not independent test implementations. They are different reductions
and calibrations of shared, independently tested primitives.

::: {.notes}
This is deliberately a montage. Do not explain every acronym. The point is the
architectural leverage and the ability to compare methods on exactly the same
scores, information conventions and simulated draws.
:::

## What did the human still have to do?

<div class="comparison">
  <div class="accent">
    <h3>The agent compounds</h3>
    <ul>
      <li>repository search and propagation</li>
      <li>implementation and build loops</li>
      <li>fixture and derivative comparisons</li>
      <li>experiment and documentation plumbing</li>
    </ul>
  </div>
  <div class="quiet">
    <h3>The researcher remains responsible</h3>
    <ul>
      <li>the estimand and mathematical contract</li>
      <li>which oracle deserves trust</li>
      <li>counterexamples and evidence standards</li>
      <li>interpretation, scope and when to stop</li>
    </ul>
  </div>
</div>

<div class="claim">AI does not remove judgment. It increases the amount of judgment you can operationalize.</div>

::: {.notes}
Avoid false modesty and false automation. The collaboration is valuable because
the researcher can encode taste, skepticism and standards into repository rules
and tests, then let the agent apply them repeatedly.
:::

## What changed?

<div class="takeaway-grid">
  <div><strong>Build engines</strong>Small explicit primitives let both people and agents reason locally and compose globally.</div>
  <div><strong>Treat tests as science</strong>When code is abundant, contracts, counterexamples and independent oracles are the scarce asset.</div>
  <div><strong>Close the loop</strong>Use agents to move from question through implementation to attempted falsification—not merely to emit code.</div>
</div>

<div class="full-quote">The revolutionary part is not that a machine can code. It is that a psychometrician can now afford to test an idea all the way down.</div>

::: {.notes}
End here. Questions can go toward Codex workflow, C++ architecture, the test
corpus, or the misspecification result.
:::

## Appendix: what exactly was counted? {.smaller}

| Metric | Definition |
|---|---|
| Canonical C++ | Physical lines in tracked C/C++ files under `include/` and `src/`; excludes dependencies, builds and vendored R copies. |
| C++ tests | Tracked C/C++ under `tests/`; test cases and assertions are doctest macro invocations. |
| JSON fixtures | Tracked `.json` files under `tests/fixtures/`. |
| Experiments | Tracked top-level directories matching `experiments/NN-*`; archived experiments are excluded. |
| Authors | Unique git author email addresses reachable from `HEAD`. |
| Days | Inclusive calendar days from the first reachable commit to render date. |

<div class="source-line">Generator: talks/oslo-psychometric-gathering-2026/tools/repo_metrics.py</div>

::: {.notes}
Use only if someone questions the numbers. The CSV also stores these definitions.
:::

## Appendix: the validation rule

<div class="full-quote">Lavaan is the oracle—until an independent reference and a first-principles property establish that it is wrong.</div>

That high bar prevents the most convenient conclusion in compatibility work:

> “Our output differs, therefore the oracle must be defective.”

::: {.notes}
The rare documented oracle defects are gated transitively or against an
independent reference. A bare difference is assumed to be a magmaan bug.
:::
